content.value_statement: Autonomous agents often fail through unclear tools, weak memory, and uncontrolled loops. This skill provides architecture patterns for safer, observable agent systems.
actual_capabilities: Explains ReAct, plan-and-execute, supervisor, and checkpoint recovery patterns.
Defines tool registry practices, tool descriptions, and execution boundaries.
Guides working, episodic, semantic, and retrieval-based memory design.
Identifies common agent failure modes and recommended safeguards.
Supports evaluation, tracing, debugging, and recovery planning for agents.
Compares single-agent and multi-agent architecture tradeoffs.
limitations: Does not provide runnable framework code or deployment scripts.
Requires project-specific validation before production use.
Does not replace security, privacy, or compliance review.
Assumes the user already understands LLM APIs and function calling.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Agent System
use_cases.description: Choose an agent loop, memory model, tool set, and oversight strategy before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing Agent
use_cases.description: Find loop risks, brittle parsing, missing observability, and weak recovery paths in an existing design.

use_cases.title: Design Multi-Agent Coordination
use_cases.description: Decide when specialist agents are justified and how a supervisor should delegate, collect, and handle failures.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Agent Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an agent architecture for this task: [describe task]. Compare ReAct, plan-and-execute, and a non-agent workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Define Tool Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed tools for an AI agent: [list tools]. Suggest clear descriptions, parameters, errors, and safety limits.

prompt_templates.title: Design Memory and Recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Design memory, checkpointing, and recovery for this long-running agent: [describe workflow]. Include what to store and when to discard data.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Multi-Agent Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this multi-agent architecture: [describe agents, tools, handoffs, and goals]. Identify failure modes, observability gaps, and simpler alternatives.

output_examples.input: Design an agent that researches customer issues and drafts support replies.
output_examples.output: Recommended architecture: one supervised agent with search, case lookup, and draft tools. Add approval gates, iteration limits, and trace logging.

output_examples.input: Review a plan for five agents that collaborate on invoice processing.
output_examples.output: The design may be too complex. Start with one agent, split extraction and approval, and add specialist agents only after measurement.

output_examples.input: Plan memory for an agent that manages recurring operations tasks.
output_examples.output: Use working memory for the active task, summaries for past runs, and retrieval for procedures. Avoid storing complete tool outputs by default.

best_practices: Set iteration limits, timeouts, token caps, and cost controls before running autonomous loops.
Give every tool clear descriptions, examples, expected errors, and recovery guidance.
Log actions, observations, tool calls, latency, and outcomes for debugging and evaluation.
anti_patterns: Do not give agents broad tool access without a task-specific selection layer.
Do not store every observation in memory without filtering or summarization.
Do not use multi-agent designs when one agent with good tools can solve the task.

faq.question: What does this skill help me design?
faq.answer: It helps design autonomous AI agents with loops, tools, memory, planning, orchestration, evaluation, and safety controls.

faq.question: Can it write full production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and review prompts. You still need implementation, tests, and deployment validation.

faq.question: When should I use a ReAct loop?
faq.answer: Use ReAct for clear step-by-step tasks where the agent can reason, call a tool, observe results, and repeat safely.

faq.question: When should I avoid multiple agents?
faq.answer: Avoid multiple agents when a single agent with focused tools can solve the task with less cost and complexity.

faq.question: How does it address safety?
faq.answer: It recommends limits, oversight, clear error handling, logging, checkpoint recovery, and careful tool boundaries.

faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
